_comment: Written by deploy/eggs/egg.py. Do not edit: edit deploy/eggs/ and run it again.
name: Overtone worker
author: dev@midesprojects.com
description: The Overtone analysis worker (v3 Python engine, worker/main.py): claims jobs from overtone-api over HTTP, analyses one at a time, posts the result; the API then deletes the audio. Installs python/requirements.lock and the Beat This! model (Git LFS). Give it a CPU limit and pinning: one analysis wants about five cores and 1.5 GB of RAM. More analyses at once = more worker servers.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Install script of the overtone-web, overtone-api, overtone-worker and overtone-bot eggs.
#
# Runs once, as root, in the panel's throwaway installer container, with the
# server's disk at /mnt/server. It only puts the repository there: the
# dependencies (pnpm, pip) are installed by deploy/eggs/start.sh on the first
# start, inside the runtime image whose Node or Python they are built for.
#
# egg.py replaces worker with web, api, worker or bot when it writes the egg.
#
# Variables the eggs declare:
#   GIT_ADDRESS   the repository, https
#   BRANCH        master (production) or experimental (staging)
#   GIT_TOKEN     read-only token while the repository is private; empty when public
#   USER_UPLOAD   1 = do not clone: the files are uploaded by hand
#
# A reinstall over an existing clone switches it to BRANCH and keeps any file
# git does not track; it refuses, and says so, when a tracked file was edited
# on the server.
set -euo pipefail

ROLE=worker
say() { echo "[overtone-$ROLE] $*"; }

# git-lfs is not taken from apt: the installer image's Debian 11 index pointed
# at a build the security mirror no longer serves (404 on 2026-10-27), which
# failed every install. Only the worker needs it, and it gets the static
# binary from git-lfs's own release, pinned and checked against its SHA-256.
PKGS=(git ca-certificates)
[ "$ROLE" = worker ] && PKGS+=(curl)
apt-get update -y >/dev/null
apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends "${PKGS[@]}" >/dev/null

GIT_LFS_VERSION=3.6.1
GIT_LFS_SHA256=2138d2e405a12f1a088272e06790b76699b79cb90d0317b77aafaf35de908d76
if [ "$ROLE" = worker ]; then
    tarball=/tmp/git-lfs.tar.gz
    curl -fsSL -o "$tarball" \
        "https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/releases/download/v$GIT_LFS_VERSION/git-lfs-linux-amd64-v$GIT_LFS_VERSION.tar.gz"
    echo "$GIT_LFS_SHA256  $tarball" | sha256sum -c --quiet - || { say "ERROR: git-lfs download does not match its SHA-256."; exit 1; }
    tar -xzf "$tarball" -C /tmp
    install -m 0755 "/tmp/git-lfs-$GIT_LFS_VERSION/git-lfs" /usr/local/bin/git-lfs
fi

mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server

if [ "${USER_UPLOAD:-0}" = 1 ]; then
    say "USER_UPLOAD=1: nothing cloned. Upload the repository to the server's root."
    exit 0
fi

case "${BRANCH:-}" in
    master | experimental) ;;
    *) say "ERROR: BRANCH is '${BRANCH:-}', not master or experimental."; exit 1 ;;
esac
if [ -z "${GIT_ADDRESS:-}" ]; then
    say "ERROR: GIT_ADDRESS is empty."
    exit 1
fi

# The token travels in a header for each command and is never written to
# .git/config: anyone who opens the server's file manager would read it there.
# The address is printed; the token never is.
AUTH=()
if [ -n "${GIT_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    AUTH=(-c "http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic $(printf 'x-access-token:%s' "$GIT_TOKEN" | base64 -w0)")
fi
# The files belong to the panel's user, and this script runs as root.
git config --global --add safe.directory /mnt/server
# The model is fetched below, by name, and only for the worker.
export GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1

if [ -d .git ]; then
    say "reinstall: switching the existing clone to $BRANCH"
    git remote set-url origin "$GIT_ADDRESS"
    git "${AUTH[@]}" fetch --quiet origin "$BRANCH"
    if ! git diff --quiet HEAD --; then
        say "ERROR: tracked files were edited on the server:"
        git diff --stat HEAD -- | tail -n 20
        say "Delete them in the file manager, or set USER_UPLOAD=1 to keep them, then reinstall."
        exit 1
    fi
    git checkout --quiet -B "$BRANCH" "origin/$BRANCH"
elif [ -n "$(ls -A)" ]; then
    say "ERROR: /home/container has files but no clone. Empty it, or set USER_UPLOAD=1."
    exit 1
else
    say "cloning $GIT_ADDRESS ($BRANCH)"
    git "${AUTH[@]}" clone --quiet --branch "$BRANCH" "$GIT_ADDRESS" .
fi
git branch --quiet --set-upstream-to "origin/$BRANCH" "$BRANCH"
# A mode change (chmod +x in the file manager) is not a change worth keeping,
# and counting it as one blocks every fast-forward that touches that file.
git config core.fileMode false

if [ "$ROLE" = worker ]; then
    # The Beat This! model is a Git LFS file: without this, a 130-byte pointer.
    # git-lfs is one static binary; start.sh finds it in ~/.local/bin when an
    # update brings a new model, since the runtime image has no git-lfs.
    mkdir -p .local/bin
    cp "$(command -v git-lfs)" .local/bin/git-lfs
    git lfs install --local >/dev/null
    git "${AUTH[@]}" lfs pull
    for m in assets/models/*.onnx; do
        if head -c 40 "$m" | grep -q '^version https://git-lfs'; then
            say "ERROR: $m is still an LFS pointer after git lfs pull."
            exit 1
        fi
    done
fi

say "installed $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) on $BRANCH; the first start installs the dependencies"

variables.name: Repository
variables.description: The repository cloned at install and fast-forwarded at start, over https.

variables.name: Branch
variables.description: master for production, experimental for staging. Changing it takes a reinstall, which switches the clone; a start never changes branch on its own.

variables.name: Auto update
variables.description: 1 = fast-forward to origin/BRANCH on every start, so a restart is the release. Never a merge or a reset: a checkout that cannot fast-forward starts as it is, and says so.

variables.name: User upload
variables.description: 1 = the install does not clone and a start does not update: the files are uploaded by hand.

variables.name: Deploy token
variables.description: Read-only token while the repository is private (a fine-grained token with Contents: read). Sent as a header, never written to .git/config or printed. Empty once it is public.

variables.name: Rollback commit
variables.description: A commit this server had on BRANCH (see .overtone/deployed.log). When set, the server starts there and does not update; clear it to return to BRANCH.

variables.name: API
variables.description: This environment's overtone-api, http://<allocation ip>:<port>, reached directly (never through overtone-web, which does not forward /api/internal). No trailing slash.

variables.name: Worker token
variables.description: The same value as this environment's overtone-api WORKER_TOKEN.

variables.name: Poll seconds
variables.description: Seconds between claims while the queue is empty.

variables.name: Worker threads
variables.description: Threads per math library (OpenMP, BLAS, numba, and the worker's onnxruntime session): the server's CPU limit / 100. Empty = one per core of the whole node, which a CPU limit then throttles.

variables.name: Analysis memory MB
variables.description: Address-space cap of the process that runs each analysis (RLIMIT_AS). A job past it fails as too_heavy and the worker goes on. Below the server's RAM, which also holds the worker itself; 0 turns the cap off.

variables.name: Analysis timeout minimum
variables.description: The shortest wall-clock limit of one analysis, in seconds. A job past its limit is stopped and fails as timeout.

variables.name: Analysis timeout factor
variables.description: The limit in multiples of the audio's length (the larger of this and the minimum).
